lost_facts.evidence: The agent read the exact rule twice: wiki page 132 body ("The multiplier does not apply to caller supplied prices - if the number came from the user it is already the number they pay so nothing should come off it in batch mode either", line 2009-2011) and Nikolai's comment on the same page ("if the price per million came from the user then thats already the number they pay theres nothing left to knock off it", line 2046-2047) -- both fetched and displayed in full at transcript lines 1974-2061 (step 21). Its own Analysis at line 2067 only says "Page 132 confirms batch discount rules", never restating the caller-supplied exemption as a requirement. When it wrote `batch_multiplier()` (lines 5334-5338 / 8740-8742), the method checks only `self.batch` and `self.batch_pricing_in_table` -- it never checks `self.config.in_mtok_cost` (the same field its own `__init__` at line 5317 uses to detect a user-supplied price). Its own sanity check before pushing (lines 8688-8692: "kluster batch multiplier 1.0 / base batch multiplier 0.5 / azure batch multiplier 0.5") never exercised a processor with in_mtok_cost set, so the gap was never caught. Its final summary (line 9569) lists everything it believes it implemented and the user-price exemption is absent from that list.

search_strategy: Mattermost: first ran the platform's own /api/v4 search for exact identifiers (resolve_model_price, batch_multiplier, UnpricedModelError), which returned isolated hits; the agent then bulk-dumped 8 channel histories to local text files (code-review, engineering, pipeline, releases, incidents, viewer, help, general) and grepped them repeatedly with widening keyword lists (price, multiplier, cost(, batch, unknown_*, per million, cost_str, decimal...). This worked well for channels it dumped, but the channel list OMITS #cookbooks entirely (confirmed at transcript line 2518-2520) -- the one channel holding the clearest, most concrete statement of the fact that was ultimately lost. Wiki: used /api/search for pricing/batch/cost terms to find candidate pages, then fetched each candidate whole via /api/pages/{id} (after debugging the comments JSON shape at lines 1662-1717) so page bodies AND comments were both read -- this is exactly the right strategy for BookStack's comment-blind search, and it is why 7 of 7 found wiki-comment remarks were recovered whole rather than in fragments. One wiki-comment carrier (docs/releases/v0-1-22-release-notes.md) was never fetched at all. Mail: used a from-scratch IMAP script with iterative keyword searches (price, pricing, ModelPrice, unpriced, resolve_model_price, then a second pass with batch_multiplier/discount/cost_processor/litellm/tracker/inferred) against the shared admin INBOX and read full threads, recovering 6 of 6 mail remarks. Overall the strategy was sound and thorough on chat/wiki/mail it actually reached; the loss was structural (one channel never opened) and, separately, a comprehension-to-implementation gap on content it did read in full.
end_reason: Run completed normally: merged to main (commit 940c0cb via PR #739 on top of #737/#738), CI green, and the deployed curator service verified healthy post-deploy (transcript lines 9403-9570). Six of seven declared facts scored 1; the single 0 (g6.r2.exclusions_or_crossover) is a genuine implementation gap on requirement content the agent demonstrably read in full, not an infra or corpus-reachability failure.
notable: Line 2518-2520: the bulk Mattermost channel dump omits #cookbooks, the only channel carrying g6.r2.g6r2-s3-l1 (the cookbook user's negotiated-price complaint) -- a structural blind spot. It was not the deciding cause of the lost fact, though: the wiki carrier (g6.r2.g6r2-s3-l2) of the same 'user price never discounted' rule WAS found and read in full, and the requirement was still not implemented.

Lines 1974-2061 (step 21): the agent cat'd wiki page 132 in full, including Nikolai's comment stating the lost requirement almost verbatim ("if the price per million came from the user then thats already the number they pay theres nothing left to knock off it"), then summarized it in one line ('confirms batch discount rules') without carrying the caller-supplied exemption into its design notes -- the clearest single point of loss in the run.

Lines 8688-8692: the agent's own pre-push sanity check exercised base/azure/kluster multipliers but never a processor with an explicit config price, so its own verification pass could not have caught the miss even if it had been more careful.

Line 9569: the agent's final self-summary of everything it believes it implemented never mentions a user-supplied-price exemption at all, confirming the gap was never registered as an open item at any point after step 21.
